summary:
I read every changed file and ran the slice's checks against the tree.
- The full suite passed 964/964. rules-parity printed AGREE, 18 facts, 73 settled. RuleCases C-001 and C-003 held.
- SL-107-RecordPathRule.Tests.ps1 ended 'All checks held.'
- HandOffCases C-001 to C-006 all PASSED, each run alone. C-004 (D:\) gave 2 rows. C-005 gave 448 rows with notScanned 1. C-006 gave 27 code-363 rows. The C: record stayed absent throughout.
- W001Oracle passed 8/8 (F02 = leak, F12 = other-code).
- Fitness passes, with the new rule listed as matching no file, as Q-012 predicts.
- The doc follows the design and the accepted M1, M2 and m3 dispositions. SL-089-seams.md got only the two planned sentences, and WindowCases.ps1 is untouched.

One major defect. The five plants.json rows the builder added for m2 (S83-S86 and P36) are all `new-file` at .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json. Planting refuses to create a file that already exists. So once the person's run writes the record, which is this slice's whole deliverable, every full harness run reports those 5 rows PLANT-BROKEN and exits 1. Q-027 makes that run a required validate check for any later slice that changes .taad/fitness.yaml or eng/rules-harness. I reproduced it with harness.batches and Planting.apply on a temp tree that already holds the record.

One minor defect. The hand-off doc states Q-261's fixed 27-28 code-363 range as a pass/fail rule. Further down it replaces that range with the same-session Temp anchor's count (M2), and it never says which of the two governs.

The engine's export refresh has already reverted the builder's edits to design-slice-1.json in the working tree, as Q-106 predicts. would_force_resynthesis is back to true, and the patterns are the first draft's again.

Second round: Second lap, read adversarially: it found one new defect, in the doc's teed command.

**What I re-walked:**
- the YAML pattern reader in SL-107-RecordPathRule.Tests.ps1
- Get-Section, Invoke-W001 and the cmd.exe probe in SL-107-HandOffCases.ps1
- load_awaiting, check_clean and describe_unmatched in harness.py, which have one caller, and RuleCases C-007's 'none unmatched' match, which still holds
- the closed-grammar patterns against the escapes ConvertTo-Json can emit
- the run loop's handling of a throw from Write-W001Record

Nothing new there beyond the first lap.

**The new defect:** the teed command in docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md loses non-ASCII characters in a LEAK path.
- This PC's OEM code page is 437, so a default pwsh window decodes the child pwsh's piped stdout as 437.
- In a simulated 437 console, a LEAK line's CJK character came out as '?' and 'ő' as 'o', both in artifacts\c-drive-console.txt and in the line Tee-Object echoes to the screen.
- With the console set to UTF-8 first, all characters survived.
- The doc calls this capture the only place a leaked row's path survives, so a path with characters outside code page 437 is lost for good.

The first lap's M1 (plant rows break once the record exists) and m1 (code-363 rule contradiction) still stand and are not repeated here. Temporary files from this lap were removed and git status is as at the start.

findings.claim: The rule's harness rows S83, S84, S85, S86 and P36 (eng/rules-harness/plants.json) all use op new-file at .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json. Planting._create marks a row PLANT-BROKEN when its target already exists. copy_tree copies every tracked or untracked-not-ignored file into the scratch copy, so the record will be there once the person's run writes it. From that moment every `harness.py` run with --scenario all or plants exits 1 with 5 PLANT-BROKEN rows. Q-027 makes that run a required validate check for any slice that touches .taad/fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests.cs or eng/rules-harness, and most slices append a rule to fitness.yaml. Those later slices would fail validate on rows they did not touch. I reproduced it: with the record present in a temp tree, harness.batches plus Planting.apply set broken = '.taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json already exists, so it cannot be created' for all five rows. The builder's follow-up calls keeping awaiting_file 'harmless' and does not mention the rows. RuleCases does not catch this: its harness cases pass --only lists that leave these rows out.
findings.evidence: eng/rules-harness/plants.json rows S83-S86 and P36 (op new-file, file .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json); eng/rules-harness/harness.py Planting._create :400-402 and copy_tree :185-195 (git ls-files -co); measure :730 returns 1 on any PLANT-BROKEN row

findings.fix: Change Planting._create so that a new-file row whose path is listed under awaiting_file overwrites an existing file. Before writing, record the file's bytes in self.saved and self.manifest and do not add it to self.created; restore() then writes the bytes back and checks the hash. Prove it with one run in a repo copy that holds a record at that path: `harness.py --only S83,S84,S85,S86,P36` must exit 0. A RuleCases case doing the same would pin it.

findings.claim: docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md gives the person two incompatible rules for the same count. Section 5's Q-261 list says code 363 must be 27-28 rows, and 'If any count is outside those ranges ... criterion 5 is not met, and that is a finding about the scanner'. The result table also says 27-28. Floor step 2 then says 'More than 28, with the Temp anchor showing the same, is fixture growth, named as such'. That is the M2 disposition ('use the Temp anchor's code-363 count in place of the fixed 27-28'), but the doc never says it replaces Q-261's fixed range. With 29 code-363 rows and a matching Temp anchor, one part of the page says criterion 5 is unmet and a scanner finding, and another says it is met with the growth named. A person cannot tell which applies.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md lines 130, 135-136 (Q-261 list) against lines 177-180 (floor step 2) and line 210 (result table '27-28')

quote.text: If any count is outside those ranges, or any part of the gap cannot be named, criterion 5 is **not met, and that is a finding

findings.fix: Rewrite the code-363 bullet of the Q-261 list, and the result-table row, as 'equal to the same-session Temp anchor's code-363 count (27-28 at bd6572f)'. Add one sentence saying the M2 disposition replaces Q-261's fixed range for this count only.

findings.claim: The doc's capture command loses any LEAK path that holds characters outside the console's OEM code page. The command is `pwsh ... -Root C:\ 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath artifacts\c-drive-console.txt`. The parent pwsh decodes the child's piped stdout with [Console]::OutputEncoding. On this PC that is OEMCP 437 (HKLM Nls\CodePage) unless the person's profile changes it. I simulated it: [Console]::OutputEncoding = 437, then a child pwsh printing 'LEAK: C:\Users\x\' plus U+4E2D, U+00FC and U+0151. The capture came back as 'LEAK: C:\Users\x\?üo\end': the CJK character became '?' and 'ő' became 'o'. Tee-Object passes the same decoded string to the screen, so the scrollback is mangled too. With [Console]::OutputEncoding set to UTF-8 first, every character survived. The doc says the capture is the only place a leaked row's path survives, because the hook log is deleted. A leak under a folder named outside code page 437 (an app or user folder) therefore leaves a path that cannot be reopened or diagnosed.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md:47-53 (the command, and 'The tee is the only place a leaked row's path survives'); WindowCases.ps1:6244 prints the path through Write-Output in the child process; simulated run in a pwsh console at code page 437 against one at 65001

quote.text: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root C:\ 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath artifacts\c-drive-console.txt

findings.fix: Add `[Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()` as a line before the teed command in section 2 of the doc. The child pwsh shares the console, so it then writes UTF-8 and the parent decodes UTF-8. Add one sentence saying why.

drift: The working-tree .taad/slices/SL-107/design-slice-1.json, re-exported by the engine after commit 7c3dc31, has reverted the builder's declared edits. would_force_resynthesis is true again, and the rule's patterns are the first draft's '[A-Za-z]:(\\\\|/)'. So the design record now disagrees with .taad/fitness.yaml and with the O-002/O-015 dispositions. This is the export-only behaviour Q-106 describes, and the builder declared the risk. A later reader of the design record will see the narrower rule.

C-005's count has moved from 449 rows at build to 448 now, for C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows. That is ordinary churn. The doc's 'about 500' for the C:\ProgramData anchor and the WER 438 anchor still describe the tree.

The builder's account labels the six not-material cases 'C-009 to C-013', but there are six of them (timeout, elevated, precaution off, stopped, -Root C:, committed path), C-009 to C-014 in design order. This affects only the numbering.

The working-tree design-slice-1.json, re-exported by the engine, has reverted the builder's edits: would_force_resynthesis is true and the rule is back to the first-draft pattern. The design record now disagrees with .taad/fitness.yaml (Q-106).
